endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Review AI system performance and impact using the monitoring and reporting plan developed in Stage II and adapted in Stage V on a consistent cadence (e.g. quarterly, yearly) to decide whether to maintain the system as deployed, refine aspects of the deployed system, or sunset (“turn off”) the system.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: The management process is structured around five specific decision gates (G1–G5) that a model must pass before and after deployment:

endorsements.title: Developing, purchasing, implementing and monitoring AI tools in radiology: practical considerations. A multi-society statement
endorsements.issuer: ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR, RSNA; Radiol Artif Intell 2024 (PMID 38251899, doi:10.1148/ryai.230513)
endorsements.quote: How will the AI tool be integrated into the institutions’ workflows and how can the commercial claims be verified and monitored?

endorsements.title: Key decision points in adopting an AI solution
endorsements.issuer: Health AI Partnership (Duke Health and partners)
endorsements.quote: This decision point features guides for monitoring AI solutions and affected work environments over time and sustaining improved outcomes achieved through AI use.

endorsements.title: Implementing Artificial Intelligence in Radiology: Design Thinking Road Map
endorsements.quote: Finally, institutions must be prepared to pause or withdraw AI tools that fail to demonstrate sustained value or that impose disproportionate burdens.

endorsements.title: Co-Lifecycle Governance for Learning Medical AI: A Hybrid Convergence Framework for Adaptive Regulatory Oversight
endorsements.quote: When surveillance and validation indicate persistent, nonmitigable risk, governance should support staged controls: conditional suspension (use restricted to defined contexts), rollback to a prior validated version, and decommissioning or recall when risks cannot be acceptably reduced.

endorsements.title: Safeguarding AI-driven digital health - An adaptation of the Swiss cheese model for safety
endorsements.quote: Defenses include live performance monitoring, drift detection, periodic benefit–risk reviews and clear triggers for retraining, revalidation, rollback and retirement.

endorsements.title: A testable framework linking diagnostic AI contribution to outcome measurement in clinical decision support
endorsements.quote: De-implementation should be treated as a normal safety function rather than as a failure of innovation [ 17 , 18 ].

endorsements.title: Chinese expert concern and consensus on applications of artificial intelligence in clinical cancer imaging
endorsements.quote: Once clinically significant performance degradation is identified, standardized protocols shall govern model recalibration, retraining, temporary suspension, or clinical decommissioning.

endorsements.title: When end users can build: AI-assisted application development and the new accountability gap in digital health
endorsements.quote: Finally, post-deployment monitoring, maintenance responsibility, and lifecycle management (including update and retirement planning) should be explicitly assigned.

endorsements.title: A five-phase evaluation framework for diagnostic and predictive medical artificial intelligence
endorsements.quote: This pathway includes clear fall-back protocols, such as automatic rollback to a prior validated version, reverting the model to background shadow-mode tracking, temporary suspension of deployment, or full withdrawal, thereby safeguarding patient care while root-cause analysis and model retraining occur.

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether periodic maintain, refine, or retire decisions, or protocols to disable, roll back, recall, or decommission AI tools, reduce continued use of harmful or obsolete tools. Support for the practice rests on 11 endorsements, most of them commentaries and frameworks, and no study documenting the hazard was supplied.

perspectives.view: Eleven sources endorse the practice. Two are CHAI frameworks rated must, one is a multi-society radiology statement, and most of the rest are commentaries. No study tests the practice or documents the hazard, so certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. Agreement among endorsers reflects expert opinion rather than measured effect.

Several commentaries describe staged controls, including conditional suspension, rollback to a prior validated version, reversion to shadow mode, and full withdrawal. They tie each control to monitoring triggers. None of these sources reports whether such protocols caught a failing tool before it harmed patients, and so the safety benefit remains an untested assumption.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare health systems with and without scheduled lifecycle reviews and decommissioning protocols. They should measure time from detected performance degradation or vendor recall to disablement, patient harms during that interval, and staff effort required to carry out rollback or retirement.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems cannot tell from this evidence whether lifecycle reviews detect degradation that falls mainly on these groups, or whether retiring a tool leaves safety-net sites without a working alternative.
